name: Ted Keenan
highlight: Keenan swam from Dover to Sangatte in 18h11 and went on to complete the English, North and Bristol Channels.
biography: Edward “Ted” Keenan trained on Lough Erne and off Bundoran. In August 1972 the 37-year-old from Enniskillen set out from Shakespeare Beach, Dover, with his son Brian aboard the escort boat. A tide change near Cap Gris-Nez carried his swim on towards Sangatte, where he came ashore the next morning.

A year later Keenan swam from Orlock Point in Northern Ireland to the Scottish coast in 18 hours 27 minutes. He completed the Original Triple Crown in July 1975 when he reached Coney Beach in Porthcawl after crossing the Bristol Channel. Brian accompanied his father on all three swims.

facts.label: Sporting country
facts.value: Ireland in the CSA result. The CS&PF historical register lists UK [Northern Ireland].

lines.label: Route and time
lines.text: Solo, England to France. Keenan left Shakespeare Beach at 15:23 on 12 August and reached Sangatte at 09:34 on 13 August. The two register clocks span 18 hours 11 minutes overnight. The register does not specify a time zone.

lines.label: Why two dates appear
lines.text: The CS&PF register and the exhibition heading give 12 August. The Irish association’s memorial uses 13 August, the finish date. The exhibition narrative also describes departure on the 13th and mixes up the weekdays.

lines.label: Escort and recognition
lines.text: The Channel Swimming Association recognises this crossing. The CS&PF register names Leonard Hutchinson as pilot, Envictor as the boat and Brian Keenan as trainer.

lines.text: 14 hours 26 minutes 15 seconds for the crossing from Glenthorne to Porthcawl. The British Long Distance Swimming Association ratified the swim.

lines.label: Route and clocks
lines.text: The family exhibition gives 06:04 at Glen Cove and 20:30 at Coney Beach and reports the duration to the minute. It identifies John Lewis as pilot and Brian Keenan as feeder.

questions.label: When did Ted Keenan swim the English Channel?
questions.value: He started on 12 August 1972 and landed in France on 13 August after 18 hours 11 minutes.

questions.label: Where did Ted Keenan land in France?
questions.value: He landed at Sangatte after starting at Shakespeare Beach in Dover.

questions.label: Which three channels did Ted Keenan swim?
questions.value: He crossed the English Channel in 1972, the North Channel in 1973 and the Bristol Channel in 1975.
